mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity present value.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the preceding month
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during high-rate periods, or the FEDFUNDS spike is not statistically associated with lower SPX returns (p > 0.05 in Granger causality).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2,000 since the previous CPIAUCSL peak coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor demand growth supports corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month increase ≥ 2,000 for two consecutive months following a CPIAUCSL local maximum
regime_hint: Early stage of a labor market recovery after a soft landing
failure_condition: Empirical power of the lagged PAYEMS change on SPX 20d returns is insignificant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests, or the effect reverses during periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 6%).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) grows by at least 5% month-over-month for three consecutive months, it predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as stronger consumer demand raises corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month growth ≥ 5% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Resuming upward momentum in consumer spending cycle
failure_condition: The three-month HOUST acceleration is not statistically predictive of SPX 60-day returns (p > 0.05 in rolling Granger test), or the effect is absent during recessions (UNRATE > 6%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) index below 110 for two consecutive months, following a prior expansionary phase, is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing momentum reduces earnings growth forecasts.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 110 for two consecutive months after a prior rise above 115
regime_hint: Early warning of a supply-side softening in the manufacturing sector
failure_condition: No significant negative effect of INDPRO declines on SPX 20d returns (p > 0.10), or the effect is reversed during periods of strong global demand (CPIAUCSL > 203).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months in a context of rising FEDFUNDS (> 5%), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a negative 60-day forward return as the real interest rate rises and growth expectations cool.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS > 5% in the same window
regime_hint: Transition to restrictive monetary policy with falling labor participation
failure_condition: The interaction of UNRATE and FEDFUNDS does not predict negative 60-day SPX returns (p > 0.05 in out-of-sample), or the effect is absent when global risk premia are low (CPIAUCSL < 205).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in RSAFS (retail and small business credit) above 400,000 in a month when UNRATE is below 5%, signals optimism in credit availability and corporate investment, leading to a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS crosses above 400,000 while UNRATE < 5% in the same month
regime_hint: Optimism in credit markets during low unemployment
failure_condition: The RSAFS/UNRATE interaction is not predictive of SPX 20d returns (p > 0.10), or the effect disappears during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 210).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month cumulative decline in GDPC1 (GDP personal consumption) of at least 2% after a prior 3-month expansion is a leading indicator of a cooling demand cycle, resulting in a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 cumulative monthly change < -2% over three consecutive months following a prior cumulative increase ≥ 2%
regime_hint: Signs of demand moderation in the consumer economy
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically different from baseline during such demand decelerations (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when inflation is low (CPIAUCSL < 200).

mechanism_narrative: When the 6-month moving average of INDPRO falls below 110 while HOUST rises by at least 10% month-over-month for two consecutive months, it indicates a supply-demand misalignment that predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO_m6 < 110 AND HOUST month-over-month increase ≥ 10% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Structural imbalance between industrial production and consumer demand
failure_condition: The combined signal does not significantly predict negative SPX 20d returns (p > 0.10), or the effect is absent when consumer confidence is weak (PAYEMS < 120,000).
